taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station BMGS-bori-field, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1005 | 3.42 | 3.42
2 | 3588 | 6.33 | 9.76
3 | 1358 | 10.9 | 20.7
4 | 333 | 9.08 | 29.7
5 | 2950 | 36.8 | 66.5
6 | 5469 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KQHA-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the VES curve type, we analyze each consecutive triplet of layer resistivities:

1. **Layers 1-2-3** ($1005 < 3588 > 1358\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$): $r_1 < r_2 > r_3 \rightarrow$ **K**
2. **Layers 2-3-4** ($3588 > 1358 > 333\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$): $r_1 > r_2 > r_3 \rightarrow$ **Q**
3. **Layers 3-4-5** ($1358 > 333 < 2950\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$): $r_1 > r_2 < r_3 \rightarrow$ **H**
4. **Layers 4-5-6** ($333 < 2950 < 5469\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$): $r_1 < r_2 < r_3 \rightarrow$ **A**

Combining these yields **KQHA**, which matches the classification on file.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "KQHA"}
